title: How to do the Chicken Dance in PE |Practicing Locomotor Movements|

observation_window.sampling: provider default; not continuous motion capture

extraction.teacher_style: The teacher uses an energetic and structured approach tailored for physical education classes. He combines upbeat music with verbal counting and intermittent locomotor movement breaks.

lesson_structure.note: Introduction to the Chicken Dance and locomotor movements in PE class.
Explaining the 4-count dance steps: beaks, wings, tail feathers, and claps.
Explaining locomotor movements like skipping, sliding, and galloping.
Practicing the routine with music alternating between dance and movement breaks.

steps_taught.name: Beaks
steps_taught.description: Four counts of beak hand gestures.

steps_taught.name: Wings
steps_taught.description: Four counts of wing hand gestures.

steps_taught.name: Tail Feathers
steps_taught.description: Four counts of tail feather wiggle.

steps_taught.name: Skip
steps_taught.description: Skipping locomotor movement in open space.

what_works: Breaking down the dance into clear four-count sections
Alternating between stationary dance steps and locomotor movement breaks

quotes.text: The Chicken Dance is a four-count dance.
First time through is a skip, second time is a slide, third time is a gallop.

evidence_segments.observation: Teacher demonstrates hand gestures for beaks, wings, tail feathers, and claps facing forward.

extraction.distinctive_method: Integrating traditional folk dance moves with PE locomotor movement intervals like skipping, sliding, and galloping.
